Attempt at machine learning algorithm to predict health outcomes based on various variables including alcohol intake and location

```{r}
# dataset for converting zipcode to town/city
zipcode_data <- read.csv("../data/4pp.csv", header = TRUE)

# Lifelines dataset
data <- read.csv("../data/Lifelines Dataset.csv ", header = TRUE, na.strings=c("NA","NaN", "")) # Convert NA, NaN and "" (blank field) to NA for uniformity
```


```{r}
# Selecting columns of interest
data_of_interest <- data %>%
  select(zip_code_T1_M,
         bodyweight_kg_all_m_1_T1_M,
         bodyweight_kg_all_m_1_T2_M,
         alcohol_intake_adu_c_1_T1_QF,
         bpavg_diastolic_all_m_1_T1_BP,
         bpavg_systolic_all_m_1_T1_BP,
         bpavg_diastolic_all_m_1_T2_BP,
         bpavg_systolic_all_m_1_T2_BP,
         cholesterol_result_all_m_1_T1_S,
         cholesterol_result_all_m_1_T2_S,
         circumference_hip_all_m_1_T1_M,
         circumference_hip_all_m_1_T2_M,
         circumference_waist_all_m_1_T1_M,
         circumference_waist_all_m_1_T2_M,
         age_1a_q_1,
         gender_T1_M)

```

As the names of the columns are quite long and thus a bit inconvenient to work with, we will rename the columns.
```{r}
data_of_interest <- data_of_interest %>%
  rename(zipcode = zip_code_T1_M,
         body_weight = bodyweight_kg_all_m_1_T1_M,
         body_weight_2 = bodyweight_kg_all_m_1_T2_M,
         bp_dia = bpavg_diastolic_all_m_1_T1_BP,
         bp_dia_2 = bpavg_diastolic_all_m_1_T2_BP,
         bp_sys = bpavg_systolic_all_m_1_T1_BP,
         bp_sys_2 = bpavg_systolic_all_m_1_T2_BP,
         cholesterol = cholesterol_result_all_m_1_T1_S,
         cholesterol_2 = cholesterol_result_all_m_1_T2_S,
         circumference_hip = circumference_hip_all_m_1_T1_M,
         circumference_hip_2 = circumference_hip_all_m_1_T2_M,
         circumference_waist = circumference_waist_all_m_1_T1_M,
         circumference_waist_2 = circumference_waist_all_m_1_T2_M,
         age = age_1a_q_1,
         gender = gender_T1_M,
         alcohol_intake = alcohol_intake_adu_c_1_T1_QF)

data_of_interest$age <- data_of_interest$age/12
data_of_interest$row_id <- 1:nrow(data_of_interest)
```


```{r}
data_of_interest <- data_of_interest %>%

```

Now there are no more missing values


```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the raw data and create the target
# -------------------------------------------------
machine_learning_data <- data_of_interest %>%
  mutate(BODYWT_GAIN = body_weight -
           body_weight_2) %>%
  mutate(WAIST_CIRC_GAIN = circumference_waist_2 -
           circumference_waist) %>%
   mutate(HIP_CIRC_GAIN = circumference_hip_2 -
           circumference_hip) %>%
  mutate(CHOLESTEROL_GAIN = cholesterol_2 -
           cholesterol) %>%
  mutate(DIA_BP_GAIN = bp_dia_2 -
           bp_dia) %>%
    mutate(SYS_BP_GAIN = bp_sys_2 -
           bp_sys)
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 2. Choose the predictors you really want
# -------------------------------------------------
predictor_vars <- c(
  "age",
  "gender",
  "alcohol_intake",
  "provincie"
)

machine_learning_data <- machine_learning_data %>% select(all_of(c(predictor_vars, "DIA_BP_GAIN")))
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 3. Split into train / test (keep the outcome with the splits)
# -------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(machine_learning_data$DIA_BP_GAIN, p = .8, list = FALSE)
train_raw <- machine_learning_data[train_idx, ]
test_raw  <- machine_learning_data[-train_idx, ]
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 4. Turn character columns into factors (needed for dummyVars)
# -------------------------------------------------
to_factor <- function(x) if (is.character(x)) as.factor(x) else x
train_raw[] <- lapply(train_raw, to_factor)
test_raw[]  <- lapply(test_raw,  to_factor)
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 5. Add an explicit “Missing” level to every factor
# -------------------------------------------------
add_missing_level <- function(dat) {
  fac_cols <- sapply(dat, is.factor)
  dat[fac_cols] <- lapply(dat[fac_cols], function(f) {
    f <- addNA(f)                     # NA becomes a level
    levels(f)[is.na(levels(f))] <- "Missing"
    f
  })
  dat
}
train_raw <- add_missing_level(train_raw)
test_raw  <- add_missing_level(test_raw)
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 6. ---------- PRE‑PROCESSING ----------
# -------------------------------------------------
# 6a. Strip the outcome before any preprocessing
train_X <- train_raw %>% select(-DIA_BP_GAIN)
test_X  <- test_raw  %>% select(-DIA_BP_GAIN)

# 6b. Impute, centre and scale *only* the predictor columns
pp_obj <- preProcess(
  train_X,
  method = c("medianImpute", "center", "scale"),
  nzv = TRUE               # drop zero‑variance (incl. all‑NA) columns
)

train_pp <- predict(pp_obj, train_X)
test_pp  <- predict(pp_obj, test_X)

# 6c. One‑hot encode the (now all‑numeric + factor) predictors
dummy_mod <- dummyVars(~ ., data = train_pp, fullRank = FALSE)

train_enc <- predict(dummy_mod, newdata = train_pp) %>% as.data.frame()
test_enc  <- predict(dummy_mod, newdata = test_pp)  %>% as.data.frame()

# 6d. Finally, re‑attach the outcome column (it never got touched)
train_enc$DIA_BP_GAIN <- train_raw$DIA_BP_GAIN
test_enc$DIA_BP_GAIN  <- test_raw$DIA_BP_GAIN
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 7. Train the neural‑net
# -------------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
nnet_grid <- expand.grid(
  size  = c(1, 5, 50),
  decay = c(0.5, 1e-7)
)

nnet_model <- train(
  DIA_BP_GAIN ~ .,
  data        = train_enc,
  method      = "nnet",
  metric      = "RMSE",
  tuneGrid    = nnet_grid,
  trControl   = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 2),
  linout      = TRUE,      # regression
  trace       = TRUE      
)

```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 8. Quick sanity‑check on the hold‑out set
# -------------------------------------------------
test_pred <- predict(nnet_model, newdata = test_enc)

rmse_test <- sqrt(mean((test_enc$DIA_BP_GAIN - test_pred)^2))
mae_test  <- mean(abs(test_enc$DIA_BP_GAIN - test_pred))
r2_test   <- cor(test_enc$DIA_BP_GAIN, test_pred)^2

cat("\n=== Test‑set performance ===\n")
cat("RMSE :", round(rmse_test, 3), "\n")
cat("MAE  :", round(mae_test, 3), "\n")
cat("R²   :", round(r2_test, 3), "\n")

ggplot(data = tibble(
  observed = test_enc$DIA_BP_GAIN,
  predicted = test_pred
),
aes(x = observed, y = predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, colour = "#2C3E50") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              colour = "#E74C3C", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs. Predicted Body‑weight Gain (Test Set)",
    x = "Observed Δ kg",
    y = "Predicted Δ kg"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 9. Save everything you’ll need for inference
# -------------------------------------------------
saveRDS(nnet_model,   "bodywt_nnet_model.rds")
saveRDS(dummy_mod,    "bodywt_dummyVars.rds")
saveRDS(pp_obj,       "bodywt_preprocess.rds")
saveRDS(predictor_vars, "bodywt_predictor_vars.rds")

```


```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 10. Helper for scoring a *single* new participant
# -------------------------------------------------
predict_bodywt_gain <- function(new_record) {
  ## 10a. Load artefacts
  model   <- readRDS("bodywt_nnet_model.rds")
  dummy   <- readRDS("bodywt_dummyVars.rds")
  pp      <- readRDS("bodywt_preprocess.rds")
  
  ## 10b. Make sure factor columns have the same levels as the training data
  new_record[] <- lapply(new_record, function(x) {
    if (is.character(x)) as.factor(x) else x
  })
  new_record <- add_missing_level(new_record)   # same helper as above
  
  ## 10c. Apply the *same* preprocessing (impute → centre → scale)
  # Note: the preProcess object was built on predictor‑only data,
  # so we can feed the raw new_record straight to it.
  new_pp <- predict(pp, new_record)
  
  ## 10d. One‑hot encode the predictors
  new_enc <- predict(dummy, new_pp) %>% as.data.frame()
  
  ## 10e. Predict the outcome
  predict(model, newdata = new_enc)
}

```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# 11. Example usage
# -------------------------------------------------
new_participant <- tibble(
  age                = 40,
  gender              = "FEMALE",   # must match a level seen in training
  alcohol_intake = 0,
  provincie = "Groningen"
)

predicted_one <- predict_bodywt_gain(new_participant)
print(predicted_one)
```
